passageText: We tend to think of technology as shiny tools and gadgets. Even if we acknowledge that technology can exist in disembodied form, such as software, we tend not to include in this category paintings, literature, music, dance, poetry, and the arts in general. But we should. If a thousand lines of letters in UNIX qualifies as a technology (the computer code for a web page), then a thousand lines of letters in English (Hamlet) must qualify as well. They both can change our behavior, alter the course of events, or enable future inventions. A Shakespeare sonnet and a Schubert symphony, then, are in the same category as Google's search engine and the smartphone: They are something useful produced by a mind. We can't separate out the multiple overlapping technologies responsible for a Lord of the Rings movie. The literary rendering of the original novel is as much an invention as the digital rendering of its fantastical creatures. Both are useful works of the human imagination. Both influence audiences powerfully. Both are technological.

'Only + 부사구'가 문두에 올 때 주어와 조동사는 반드시 도치되어야 하므로 'you can'은 비문입니다. 다른 해석으로 보아도 'Only by doing this'가 주어역할을 할 수 없으므로 무조건 도치가 일어나야 합니다.

answer.surroundingText: Only by doing this can you create an interested audience that you will then be able to sell to.

question.passageWithMarkers: You already have a business and you're about to launch your blog __(A) so that__ you can sell your product. Unfortunately, here is where a 'business mind' can be a bad thing. Most people believe that to have a successful business blog promoting a product, they have to stay strictly 'on the topic.' If all you're doing is shamelessly promoting your product, then who is going to want to read the latest thing you're __(B) writing__ about? Instead, you need to give some useful or entertaining information away for free so that people have a reason to __(C) keep__ coming back. Only by doing this __(D) you can__ create an interested audience that you will then be able to sell to. passageText: You already have a business and you're about to launch your blog so that you can sell your product. Unfortunately, here is where a 'business mind' can be a bad thing. Most people believe that to have a successful business blog promoting a product, they have to stay strictly 'on the topic.' If all you're doing is shamelessly promoting your product, then who is going to want to read the latest thing you're writing about? Instead, you need to give some useful or entertaining information away for free so that people have a reason to keep coming back. Only by doing this can you create an interested audience that you will then be able to sell to. So, the best way to be successful with a business blog is to write about things that your audience will be interested in.

answerStage.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
answerStage.answerDesign: 정답 문장은 'They maintain that if a tree fell in a forest and no one was there to see it, its leaves would be colorless...'입니다. 본문에서는 현재 실현 가능성이 박약하거나 반대되는 상황을 가정한 'if + 주어 + 과거동사(fell), 주어 + 조동사 과거형 + 동사원형(would be)'의 가정법 과거 구문을 사용하고 있습니다. 이 중 fell을 현재시제인 falls로 바꿀 경우, 주절의 would be와 시제/가정법 호응이 이루어지지 않아 비문이 됩니다. 이는 조건절과 주절의 서법 조화 규칙에 위배되는 전형적인 수능형 가정법 출제 포인트입니다.

answer.surroundingText: They maintain that if a tree fell in a forest and no one was there to see it, its leaves would be colorless - and so would everything else.

answerStage.explanation: if절에 과거동사 fell이 쓰이고 주절에 'would + 동사원형(would be)'이 쓰인 가정법 과거 문장입니다. 현재 사실과 반대되거나 실현 가능성이 희박한 상황을 가정하고 있으므로, 조건절의 동사 자리에 현재형 falls를 쓰면 주절의 조동사 과거형 would와 호응하지 않아 어법상 틀린 문장이 됩니다. 따라서 falls를 과거형인 fell로 고쳐야 올바른 가정법 과거 구문이 완성됩니다.

(A) 동격의 접속사 — 완전한 절을 이끄는 명사 동격 기능 판정
(B) 보어 자리의 형용사 — 원급 비교 구문 안에서 형용사/부사 선택
question.passageWithMarkers: Many people take the commonsense view __(A) that__ color is an objective property of things, or of the light that bounces off them. They say a tree's leaves are green because they reflect green light - a greenness that is just as __(B) real__ as the leaves. Others argue that color doesn't inhabit the physical world at all but exists only in the eye or mind of the viewer. They maintain that if a tree __(C) falls__ in a forest and no one was there to see it, its leaves would be colorless - and so would everything else. They say there is no such thing as color; there __(D) are__ only the people who see it. Both positions are, in a way, correct. Color is objective and subjective - "the place," as Paul Cézanne put it, "where our brain and the universe meet." Color is __(E) created__ when light from the world is registered by the eyes and interpreted by the brain.

passageText: Many people take the commonsense view that color is an objective property of things, or of the light that bounces off them. They say a tree's leaves are green because they reflect green light - a greenness that is just as real as the leaves. Others argue that color doesn't inhabit the physical world at all but exists only in the eye or mind of the viewer. They maintain that if a tree fell in a forest and no one was there to see it, its leaves would be colorless - and so would everything else. They say there is no such thing as color; there are only the people who see it. Both positions are, in a way, correct. Color is objective and subjective - "the place," as Paul Cézanne put it, "where our brain and the universe meet." Color is created when light from the world is registered by the eyes and interpreted by the brain.

question.passageWithMarkers: Unfortunately, many people don't take personal responsibility for their own growth. Instead, they simply run the race __(A) laid out__ for them. They do well enough in school to keep advancing. Maybe they manage to get a good job at a well-run company. But so many think and act __(B) as if__ their learning journey ends with college. They have checked all the boxes in the life that was laid out for them and now __(C) lacking__ a road map describing the right ways to move forward and continue to grow. In truth, that's when the journey really begins. When school is finished, your growth becomes __(D) voluntary__. passageText: Whether or not we can catch up on sleep - on the weekend, say - is a hotly debated topic among sleep researchers; the latest evidence suggests that while it isn't ideal, it might help. When Peter Liu, a UCLA sleep researcher, brought chronically sleep-restricted people into the lab for a weekend of sleep during which they slept about 10 hours per night, they showed improvements in the ability of insulin to process blood sugar. That suggests that catch-up sleep may undo some but not all of the damage that sleep deprivation causes, which is encouraging given how many adults don't get the hours they need each night. Still, Liu isn't ready to endorse the habit of sleeping less and making up for it later. "It's like telling people you only need to eat healthy during the weekends, but during the week you can eat whatever you like," he says.

answerStage.answerDesign: 정답 문장은 'But he was in such a hurry, knowing he was dying, that he forgot to give them knees...'입니다. 여기서 분사구문 'knowing'을 정동사 형태인 'knew'로 오형 변형합니다. 'knowing he was dying'은 문맥상 주어인 'he'의 상태를 부가 수식하는 분사구문 혹은 주절에 삽입된 분사절이어야 하는데, 이를 접속사 없이 정동사 'knew'로 바꾸면 'he was in such a hurry, knew he was dying, that...'이 되어 접속사 없이 두 개의 정동사가 나열되는 통사적 오류(Run-on sentence)가 발생합니다. 다른 해석을 적용하더라도 타동사 knew의 목적어절이 이미 존재하므로 접속사 없는 동사 중복 비문을 피할 수 없습니다.

answer.surroundingText: But he was in such a hurry, knowing he was dying, that he forgot to give them knees; and he absent-mindedly gave them big tails like kangaroos, which meant they couldn't sit down.

answerStage.explanation: 주절의 동사 'was'와 연결되는 접속사가 없는 상태에서 뒤이어 'knew'라는 정동사가 올 수 없습니다. 생략된 접속사(as/because 등)와 주어(he) 역할을 대신하며 문맥상 능동의 상태를 나타내도록 준동사인 분사구문 'knowing'으로 고쳐야 어법상 적절합니다.

answerStage.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
answerStage.answerDesign: 정답 문장은 'The point to remember is that sometimes in arguments the other person is trying to get you to be angry.'입니다. 여기서 be angry 자리를 'to be'를 준동사 목적격보어(get + 목적어 + to-v) 형태로 요구하는 동사 get의 어법적 특성을 이용해, 형용사 angry를 부사인 angrily로 바꾸는 오형태를 만듭니다(to be angrily). 이 경우 Linking verb인 be의 보어 자리에 부사가 오게 되므로 문법적으로 명백한 비문이 됩니다. 보어가 빠진 be 동사 뒤에 부사가 오는 구조는 한국어 번역('화나게 행동하다' 등)으로 인해 그럴듯하게 해석될 수 있으나, 통사적으로 온전한 2형식 보어 자리를 채우지 못하므로 오답입니다.

answer.surroundingText: The point to remember is that sometimes in arguments the other person is trying to get you to be angry.

answerStage.explanation: get은 목적격 보어로 to부정사(to be)를 취하며, 이때 be는 대표적인 연결동사(linking verb)이므로 뒤이어 형용사 보어가 와야 합니다. 따라서 'to be' 뒤에 부사 angrily가 오면 문법적으로 틀린 문장이 되며, 형용사인 angry로 고쳐 써야 올바른 문장이 됩니다. 한국어로는 '당신을 화나게 만들다'로 번역되어 부사가 자연스러워 보일 수 있으므로 주의해야 합니다.

passageText: We all know that tempers are one of the first things lost in many arguments. It's easy to say one should keep cool, but how do you do it? The point to remember is that sometimes in arguments the other person is trying to get you to be angry. They may be saying things that are intentionally designed to annoy you. A remark may be made to cause your anger, but responding with a cool answer that focuses on the issue raised is likely to be most effective. Indeed, any attentive listener will admire the fact that you didn't "rise to the bait."

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 앞의 명사 'precautions'를 수식하여 '~할 예방 조치'라는 의미를 나타내는형용사적 용법의 to부정사 'to prevent'는 어법상 옳습니다.

wrongOptionExplanations.(D): 주어 'we'가 환경의 바람에 의해 '이끌려 다니는' 수동의 관계에 있으므로 과거분사 'driven'으로 시작하는 분사구문은 어법상 옳습니다.

keyPoints: (E) 정동사 vs 준동사 — 문장의 주어와 수식어구를 분석하여 정동사 자리임을 판정
(B) 분사구문의 능동 vs 수동 — 의미상 주어와의 능동 관계를 확인하여 현재분사 판정
(D) 분사구문의 수동 — 생략된 주어 'we'가 행위를 당하는 대상이므로 과거분사 판정
question.passageWithMarkers: We say to ourselves: “There is plenty of time. I’ll manage somehow or other when the time comes for action.” We are rather proud of our ability to meet emergencies. So we do not plan and take precautions __(A) to prevent__ emergencies from arising. It is too easy to drift through school and college, __(B) taking__ the traditional, conventional studies that others take, following the lines of least resistance, electing “snap courses,” and going with the crowd. It is too easy to take the attitude: “First I will get my education and develop myself, and then I will know better what I __(C) am fitted__ to do for a life work.” And so we drift, __(D) driven__ by the winds of circumstance, tossed about by the waves of tradition and custom. Eventually, most men find they must be satisfied with “any port in a storm.” Sailors who select a port because they are driven to it __(E) having__ scarcely one chance in a thousand of dropping anchor in the right one.

passageText: We say to ourselves: “There is plenty of time. I’ll manage somehow or other when the time comes for action.” We are rather proud of our ability to meet emergencies. So we do not plan and take precautions to prevent emergencies from arising. It is too easy to drift through school and college, taking the traditional, conventional studies that others take, following the lines of least resistance, electing “snap courses,” and going with the crowd. It is too easy to take the attitude: “First I will get my education and develop myself, and then I will know better what I am fitted to do for a life work.” And so we drift, driven by the winds of circumstance, tossed about by the waves of tradition and custom. Eventually, most men find they must be satisfied with “any port in a storm.” Sailors who select a port because they are driven to it have scarcely one chance in a thousand of dropping anchor in the right one.

answerStage.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
answerStage.answerDesign: 정답 문장은 'If glaciers started re-forming, they have a great deal more water now to draw on ~' 부분입니다. 여기서 현재시제 'have'를 과거시제 'had'로 고쳐야 합니다. 'If' 조건절에 과거동사 'started'가 쓰였고, 주절의 조동사 역시 'would grow'로 가정법 과거 패턴을 취하고 있으나, 현재 사실의 반대나 실현 가능성이 희박한 가정을 나타내므로 주절의 조동사(would)에 선행하는 'they have' 부분은 가정법 법칙 및 서법 조화상 'they had'가 되어야 문맥에 맞습니다. if절의 시제가 과거이므로 'have'는 일차적인 시제 오류 및 비문을 형성합니다. 반증 검사 결과, 'they have'로 쓰면 단순 조건문과 가정법이 뒤섞여 비문법적인 문장이 됩니다.

answer.surroundingText: If glaciers started re-forming, they have a great deal more water now to draw on ― Hudson Bay, the Great Lakes, the hundreds of thousands of lakes of Canada, none of which existed to fuel the last ice sheet ― so they would grow very much quicker.

answerStage.explanation: 해당 문장은 현재의 사실과 반대되거나 실현 가능성이 희박한 일을 가정하는 가정법 과거 구문입니다. 조건절에 과거동사 'started'가 사용되었고, 뒤따르는 귀결절에서도 'would grow'가 쓰인 흐름에 맞추어야 합니다. 따라서 'they have'는 조건절의 서법 및 시제 흐름과 일치하지 않는 비문입니다. 지문에서는 실제 현실의 넘쳐나는 물의 양을 '현재 가지고 있다'는 직설법적 사실로 진술하는 흐름이므로 원문은 'they have'를 썼으나, 문맥상 전체 구조가 가정법 지배를 받는 조건절-귀결절 구조 속에 놓여 어법 시험에서 이를 가정법 과거 시제 일치 규칙(had)으로 고치는 문제로 출제할 경우 수험생들이 혼란을 겪기 쉬운 고난도 킬러 문항이 됩니다.

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

markedExpressions.surroundingText: If glaciers started re-forming, they have a great deal more water now to draw on

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: If glaciers started re-forming, they have a great deal more water now to draw on ― Hudson Bay, the Great Lakes, the hundreds of thousands of lakes of Canada, none of which existed to fuel the last ice sheet ― so they would grow very much quicker.

markedExpressions.label: (C)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: the hundreds of thousands of lakes of Canada, none of which existed to fuel the last ice sheet

markedExpressions.label: (D)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: In 1964, the largest earthquake ever recorded in North America rocked Alaska

markedExpressions.label: (E)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: The quake devastated 24,000 square miles of wilderness, much of it glaciated.

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 동사 start는 목적어로 동명사(v-ing)와 to-inf를 모두 취할 수 있으므로, 're-forming'은 어법상 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): 앞에 있는 명사구들을 선행사로 삼으며, 접속사 없이 독립된 명사구를 연결하기 위해 'none of whom/which' 형태의 관계대명사가 쓰인 구조이므로 'none of which'는 어법상 옳습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(D): 명사구 'the largest earthquake'를 수동의 의미로 수식하는 과거분사 형용사구이므로 'recorded'는 올바른 표현입니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(E): 앞에 나온 단수 명사 'wilderness'를 가리키는 대명사 'it'과 수량 표현이 결합한 분사구문(대명사 주어 + 형용사) 구조로 'much of it'은 문법적으로 완벽히 맞습니다.

question.explanation: (B) "had"는 어법상 틀린 표현이며 "have"로 고쳐야 한다. 이 문장은 전체적으로 'If glaciers started... they would grow...' 형태의 가정법 과거 틀을 유지하고 있지만, 중간에 삽입된 절은 빙하가 다시 형성될 경우 사용할 수 있는 수자원의 '실제 현존하는 양'을 직설법 사실로 진술하는 대목입니다. 따라서 이 부분은 현재 시점의 객관적 사실관계와 현존 상태를 나타내는 부사 'now'와 결합하여 직설법 현재 시제인 'have'를 유지해야 합니다.
keyPoints: (B) 가정법과 직설법의 혼용 — 맥락에 따른 시제 판단
(C) 관계대명사의 한정적 수식 — 대명사 vs 관계사 구분
(E) 대명사의 수일치 및 독립분사구문 주어 — 단수 wilderness 지칭 여부
question.passageWithMarkers: Here's an interesting thought. If glaciers started __(A) re-forming__, they __(B) had__ a great deal more water now to draw on ― Hudson Bay, the Great Lakes, the hundreds of thousands of lakes of Canada, __(C) none of which__ existed to fuel the last ice sheet ― so they would grow very much quicker. And if they did start to advance again, what exactly would we do? Blast them with TNT or maybe nuclear missiles? Well, doubtless we would, but consider this. In 1964, the largest earthquake ever __(D) recorded__ in North America rocked Alaska with 200,000 megatons of concentrated might, the equivalent of 2,000 nuclear bombs. Almost 3,000 miles away in Texas, water sloshed out of swimming pools. A street in Anchorage fell twenty feet. The quake devastated 24,000 square miles of wilderness, __(E) much of it__ glaciated. And what effect did all this might have on Alaska's glaciers? None.

passageText: Here's an interesting thought. If glaciers started re-forming, they have a great deal more water now to draw on ― Hudson Bay, the Great Lakes, the hundreds of thousands of lakes of Canada, none of which existed to fuel the last ice sheet ― so they would grow very much quicker. And if they did start to advance again, what exactly would we do? Blast them with TNT or maybe nuclear missiles? Well, doubtless we would, but consider this. In 1964, the largest earthquake ever recorded in North America rocked Alaska with 200,000 megatons of concentrated might, the equivalent of 2,000 nuclear bombs. Almost 3,000 miles away in Texas, water sloshed out of swimming pools. A street in Anchorage fell twenty feet. The quake devastated 24,000 square miles of wilderness, much of it glaciated. And what effect did all this might have on Alaska's glaciers? None.
